Heading: FAQs

items.title: In-House Design Team
items.text: Your project is handled by our in-house design team, helping keep communication, quality checks and delivery coordinated.

items.title: Consistent Design Support
items.text: Work with a team that understands your brief and can support related brand assets when your requirements grow.

items.title: Confidential File Handling
items.text: Your logo concepts, business information and working files are handled within the agreed project workflow.

items.title: Clear Scope and Pricing
items.text: Deliverables, revision rounds, timelines and project pricing are agreed before design work begins.

items.title: Logo Types We Design
points: Wordmarks: Where the business name itself forms the logo, as with Google.
Lettermarks: Built from initials for longer company names.
Pictorial & Icon Marks: A single recognisable symbol representing your identity.
Abstract Marks: A custom shape that represents the brand personality.
Mascot Logos: A character that gives the brand a distinct, approachable face.
Combination Marks: A name and symbol designed to work together seamlessly.

items.title: What You Receive
points: A choice of initial concepts to review and evaluate.
Primary, horizontal, stacked and single-colour versions for every placement.
Every format you need: AI, EPS, SVG, PDF, PNG and JPG.
Colour codes for print and digital (CMYK, RGB, HEX, Pantone®) so the logo stays consistent across media.
A short usage guide explaining clear space, minimum sizing and how to apply the logo correctly.

items.title: 1. Understanding Your Brand
items.text: We begin with a short brief covering what you do, who you serve, and how you want your business to be seen.

items.title: 2. Concept Development
items.text: We design a set of initial logo concepts, each with a clear reason behind it, and share them for your review.

items.title: 3. Your Feedback
items.text: You tell us which concepts work and which do not, and we talk through the options and directions together.

items.title: 4. Refinement
items.text: We develop your chosen concept, adjusting the type, colour and spacing until the logo is right for your brand.

items.title: 5. Final Delivery
items.text: We prepare every version and file format you need, along with your colour codes and a short usage guide.

items.title: 6. Beyond the Logo
items.text: Where you want it, we carry the new logo into the rest of your branding, from stationery to social media.

items: What is included in your logo design services?

You also choose from either a selection of original ideas or your chosen idea fully refined into a logo, which we deliver to you in every format possible. In addition to our basic/horizontal and mono options and your colours and brief usage info, the source files will all be included.
How much does professional logo design cost?

Depending on the size of the project: a solo logo, or a logo together with a broader visual identity. Once you’ve defined this need, you'll know exactly what to pay from one of our logo packages – no hidden extra charges when the work is done.
How long does the logo design process take?
Logos generally take 1 to 2 weeks to finalize based on the number of concepts and rounds of revision. We will agree with you on the project turnaround time and stick to it.
Do you offer logo design for small businesses and startups?

Definitely. A good portion of the logos we produce are for start-ups and expanding small businesses. We make the logo process straightforward and our logo pricing affordable so a first logo is manageable rather than daunting.
What file formats will I receive with my logo?
Vector files (AI, EPS, SVG and PDF) for printing and scaling to any size, and image files (PNG and JPG) for everyday digital use. CorelDRAW (CDR) files are available if your printer requires them.
Can you redesign or refresh an existing logo?

Depending on the brand, we might refresh an old one, keeping what our customers know and are used to, or start one from scratch if the brand has outgrown it. We start off looking at the pros and cons of the current logomark, the symbol, image, or graphic form.
What tools do you use in logo design?
Primarily Adobe Illustrator, so the logo is built as vector artwork that stays sharp at any size, supported by Photoshop for mockups and CorelDRAW where CDR files are needed.

items.title: Brand Identity & Design
items.text: We bring logos, colours, typography, imagery and brand language together into one consistent system for print, screen and everyday touchpoints.

items.title: Marketing and Sales Collaterals
items.text: We design brochures, presentations, proposals, product sheets and case studies that keep sales and marketing materials clear and on-brand.

items.title: Packaging Design

items.title: Campaign Concepts & Ad Creatives
items.text: We shape the campaign idea, then carry it across banners, video and social creative so every format feels connected.

items.title: Corporate Communication
items.text: We align communication for employees, customers, investors and the public through clear strategy, messaging and supporting materials.

items.title: Visual Identity Systems
items.text: We unify colour, typography, imagery and graphic style, then define usage rules to keep every touchpoint consistent.

items.title: PPT Design
items.text: We structure and design clear presentations for sales, company profiles, pitches and internal communication, with reusable templates where needed.

items.title: Advertising Services
items.text: We connect advertising strategy, creative, media and reporting so campaigns work toward a shared goal across platforms.

items.title: UI/UX Design
items.text: We design digital experiences around user needs and business goals, from research and user flows to interfaces and prototypes.
